free_tier.stated: Open Source: 'Always free', 'Unlimited users and locations - core features.' Business: 'free up to 10 users and 1 location.'

egress.terms: No byte allowance anywhere in the plan table; the plans meter users and locations.; ingress: none

interface_detail: web admin plus the desktop client
tooling: defguard server, defguard desktop client, standard WireGuard configs
chaining: a control plane for a user's own WireGuard mesh; it composes with a public ingress on the same VPS

limits.value: The published caps are users and locations, for which the vocabulary has no token; request-rate is the nearest. Nothing counts bytes, and there is no public listener to spend them through.

binding_note: The published caps are users and locations, for which the vocabulary has no token; request-rate is the nearest. Nothing counts bytes, and there is no public listener to spend them through.

identity_cost.detail: self-hosted: the Open Source plan needs no vendor account; the Business plan is a hosted or licensed deployment with its own admin

reliability_note: the Open Source plan is self-run, so uptime and key rotation are local work
confidence_note: Reading the gateway documentation would establish whether Defguard's own gateway can bind a public port; the VPN-server model suggests not.

evidence.proved: Open Source is 'Always free' with 'Unlimited users and locations'; Business is 'free up to 10 users and 1 location'
'Zero-touch Desktop Client Provisioning' and 'Client configuration update based on tokens', the mechanism that issues WireGuard configs

notes: The most WireGuard-native name and the least useful for it: it hands out .conf files for a private VPN, and its own gateway is not a public reverse proxy. Worth recording because a reader searching for 'WireGuard' will land here.

extras.wg_detail: Defguard provisions a user's tunnel: 'Zero-touch Desktop Client Provisioning' and 'Client configuration update based on tokens'. The product is a WireGuard control plane, which is the one place where a standard client config is the deliverable.
extras.volume_stated: No byte allowance anywhere in the plan table; the plans meter users and locations.
extras.transit_note: peers reach each other over the WireGuard tunnels Defguard configures; the server sees handshakes, not payload
